summary: The product intent, two-role Harness, wave limits, six-dimension stance, safety boundary, prompt family, and donor-code diagnosis are largely coherent, but a fresh engineering Agent cannot responsibly start TASK-008. The work map still selects open TASK-007, and the frozen disk truth leaves core TASK-008 decisions undefined or contradictory: pre-code prompt evaluation is circular with TASK-010; the state/event persistence protocol has no executable transition or event-envelope contract; exact source revision identity is lost in several reference fields; route-readiness waiver semantics lack a truth table; canonical schemas drift from recorded decisions and capability requirements; and TASK-008 omits the exact donor reads and runnable contract-test command needed to preserve existing behavior.

gaps.gap: The pre-code gate is circular. `.loom/PROJECT.md:106-116` requires prompt eval thresholds before coding, and `.loom/DECISIONS.md:195-201` says the entire Prompt v3 family must be evaluated before any runtime migration. But `.loom/tasks.json:565-609` makes TASK-008 the schema/state migration, while `.loom/tasks.json:663-709` defers real-model Prompt v3 evaluation to TASK-010 after TASK-008 and TASK-009; `prompts/PROMPT-ARCHITECTURE.md:114-123` also says prompt activation waits for matching schema/state plus a real-model report.
gaps.why_it_blocks_start: A fresh Agent cannot tell whether TASK-008 is authorized now, or whether it must first produce an evaluation that cannot run against the not-yet-implemented schema/context/state machine. Either choice violates a current gate.
gaps.evidence_to_close: Choose and record one non-circular gate. The likely closure is to state that pre-code requires cross-document harmony, executable fixture specifications, and Keeper pass, while real-model evaluation/activation occurs only after TASK-008/009 provide the matching runtime; update PROJECT, the current decision, acceptance pre-code gate, Prompt Architecture, and task dependencies consistently. Alternatively move a genuinely runnable schema/context/eval slice before TASK-008. Then prepare a changed digest.

gaps.gap: The canonical Harness names states and events but does not define the event model TASK-008 is supposed to implement. `.loom/design/conversational-six-dimension-harness.md:256-294` lists top-level states and event names only; `.loom/design/acceptance-and-research.md:82-94` requires a top-level transition table; `.loom/tasks.json:565-609` requires an event model, XState, transactional revisions, pause/resume, degraded and safety behavior. No canonical document defines legal source-state/event/target-state transitions, event envelope and payload schemas, proposal-to-commit correlation, event/snapshot persistence, duplicate-delivery semantics, resume history, or degraded/safety recovery rules. Route-intent, ordinary-day, plan and trial transitions also have no named events.
gaps.why_it_blocks_start: These are product-integrity decisions, not interchangeable implementation details. Different reasonable implementations would disagree about whether a retry can commit, what RESUMED restores, whether safety_stop is terminal, how a proposed artifact maps to a committed event, and how database revision and XState snapshot stay atomic.
gaps.evidence_to_close: Add a canonical transition table and versioned `EventEnvelope`/payload contracts covering every documented top-level and nested state, including allowed origin, guards, target, idempotency key, base/session revision, proposal/commit correlation, transaction boundary, persisted event/snapshot form, retry/duplicate handling, pause history, degraded recovery and safety exit policy. Add route/future/trial events or explicitly defer those states from TASK-008. Provide table/property tests generated from that contract.

gaps.gap: The exact-revision invariant contradicts several canonical reference shapes. `.loom/design/insight-plan-contracts.md:30-60` says every derived object records exact source revision and defines `EvidenceLink(source_id, source_revision)`, but `RadarDelta.source_ids` at :91-97, `WaveMission.known_source_ids` at :151-160, `ElicitationUnit.source_ids` at :223-229, memory operations such as `reason_source_id` at :290-296, and `RouteReadiness.source_ids` at :344-356 discard revisions. The same file says editing creates a new source revision at :262, but does not define whether `s-11@2` is a new row with the same logical id, a new unique id, or an in-place version; F11 assumes the same logical id across revisions.
gaps.why_it_blocks_start: TASK-008 must implement exact stale propagation and transactionally preserve revisions. Without a canonical identity/version model, an engineer must invent primary keys, uniqueness constraints, reference validation and deletion behavior, and can easily allow stale evidence to remain active.
gaps.evidence_to_close: Define the source-version persistence identity explicitly (for example logical source id plus composite revision key, immutable version rows, one active head) and use a single exact `SourceRef`/`EvidenceLink` shape everywhere a source supports or invalidates a derived object. Specify supersede/delete transactions and transitive stale propagation. Add contract tests for `s@1 -> s@2`, cross-tenant refs, deleted heads, retries and rollback.

gaps.gap: Route-readiness and provisional waiver semantics are not executable. `.loom/design/conversational-six-dimension-harness.md:92-119` and `.loom/design/adaptive-interview-system.md:207-220` mix formal readiness with the option to proceed provisionally when four dimensions are not grounded. `.loom/design/insight-plan-contracts.md:344-360` exposes `met | unmet | waived_by_user | not_applicable` plus `formal_ready`, but gives no truth table for which gates may be waived, whether a waiver can ever make `formal_ready=true`, or how `not_applicable` is treated.
gaps.why_it_blocks_start: TASK-008 explicitly owns the readiness Zod contract and guards. A fresh Agent cannot implement the boolean deterministically without guessing whether provisional consent satisfies formal readiness or merely authorizes a separate provisional path.
gaps.evidence_to_close: Publish a gate truth table/function: required formal gates, allowed `not_applicable` gates, provisional-only waivers, non-waivable safety, output fields such as `formal_ready` and `provisional_allowed`, and fifth-wave behavior. Add exhaustive table tests for all status combinations and explicit user preview/waiver events.

gaps.gap: Current user-intent/capability records disagree with the canonical artifact schemas. `.loom/DECISIONS.md:150-157` says the current ParallelLife v2 deliberately removed `gain/loss/evidence` in favor of `attractions/costs_and_tradeoffs/evidence_for`, while `.loom/design/insight-plan-contracts.md:415-443`, `.loom/design/acceptance-and-research.md:65`, and `.loom/tasks.json:716-722` restore `gains/losses/evidence` without a superseding decision. `.loom/DECISIONS.md:132-138` requires stored `trial_status` and `pause_or_exit_note`, while the canonical `Prototype` at `.loom/design/insight-plan-contracts.md:452-471` instead has `adjust_signal/stop_signal` and no trial status. `.loom/capabilities/product-design.md:46` and `.loom/capabilities/privacy-ai-safety.md:53` require insight `status=tentative`, generated/correction state, while canonical `ImmediateInsight` at `.loom/design/insight-plan-contracts.md:299-318` uses `language_strength` and a separate calibration event.
gaps.why_it_blocks_start: TASK-008 must create Zod schemas and persistence that later Tasks consume. The Agent cannot know whether canonical v3 intentionally supersedes the recorded user decisions, whether compatibility fields must be migrated, or whether capability-required metadata belongs on the insight or a separate artifact/event.
gaps.evidence_to_close: Record explicit superseding decisions and align DECISIONS, capability dossiers, canonical contracts, prompts and downstream Tasks on one field set. Define migration/compatibility behavior for existing v2 donor artifacts, including trial lifecycle and insight metadata/calibration ownership. Cross-document lint should fail on future field-name/cardinality drift.

gaps.gap: TASK-008 is not restartable from its declared reads or verification surface. `.loom/tasks.json:583-600` names only design/capability reads and broad touch directories, even though its next action is donor inventory and its done conditions promise preservation of guest, consent, upload isolation, tenant ownership and cleanup. The necessary donor files are not named: at minimum `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `prisma/schema.prisma`, `app/api/wave/route.ts`, `lib/interview/templates.ts`, `lib/ai/interviewer.ts`, `lib/ai/sensemaker/wave.ts`, `lib/ai/sensemaker/build-wave-patch.ts`, `lib/ai/sensemaker/final.ts`, `lib/working-memory/{types,schema,store,operations}.ts`, `lib/auth/session.ts`, relevant upload/session routes, and donor integration tests. It also expects `tests/contracts/`, but `playwright.config.ts:15-37` runs only e2e and integration patterns and `package.json:7-13` defines no contract/property-test command.
gaps.why_it_blocks_start: A fresh Agent must discover the migration surface, decide which donor tests constitute preservation evidence, choose a unit/property framework, and invent the completion commands. That violates LOOM's exact-read/exact-evidence handoff requirement and risks silently breaking the stable donor.
gaps.evidence_to_close: Update TASK-008 with exact source/fixture reads, exact expected file touches or migration artifacts, the first concrete command/edit, the chosen contract/property test runner, scripts/config that actually include `tests/contracts`, and reproducible evidence commands. Name the donor regression set explicitly (`guest-session`, `upload-boundary`, tenant isolation, cleanup, relevant wave tests), plus typecheck/lint/build and migration verification. After the Keeper gaps are absorbed, complete TASK-007 with evidence so `loom task next` selects TASK-008.

gaps.gap: The capability map omits the professional field that materially governs TASK-008: application/statechart architecture and transactional data integrity. The existing eight dossiers cover product, UI/UX, visual, game, conversational AI, conversation psychology, life design and privacy/safety, but none owns event-sourcing versus snapshot decisions, XState serialization, optimistic concurrency, idempotency, transaction isolation or failure recovery. Those decisions are currently scattered or absent in `.loom/design/conversational-six-dimension-harness.md`, `.loom/design/platform-and-assets.md` and `.loom/design/insight-plan-contracts.md`.
gaps.why_it_blocks_start: Conversational AI and privacy can constrain the behavior but cannot substitute for a project-specific state-machine/data-integrity stance. The missing field is exactly where the event, revision and recovery ambiguities arise, so a fresh implementer has no professional decision basis for the highest-risk slice.
gaps.evidence_to_close: Add separate project-specific capability dossier(s) for application/statechart architecture and, if treated distinctly, database/data-integrity engineering; or explicitly justify and assign those responsibilities to an existing recognized field. Each must state the selected persistence/concurrency approach, rejected alternatives, failure modes and observable proof, and the affected design contract must synthesize those judgments.

evidence: `rtk loom context --keeper` restored attempt 5 and the frozen digest; `rtk loom check` returned healthy structurally, but does not resolve the semantic contradictions above.
`rtk loom task next` returns TASK-007, whose status is open and evidence is empty; `rtk loom task get TASK-008` confirms it depends on TASK-007 and declares only seven design/capability reads.
All `.loom/tasks.json`, `.loom/state.json`, task update and harness JSON files parse successfully with Node, so the verdict is not caused by corrupt state.

`.loom/PROJECT.md` and all ten linked design documents were opened from disk; all eight capability dossiers and all eight prompt files were opened. The intended result is a guest-first mobile Next.js conversation with 3 default/5 maximum waves, 5-10 elicitation units, 1-3-question microbatches, six qualitative radar states, route intents, ordinary-day screening, three equal three-year lives and reversible three-day trials.

The professional fields currently represented are product design, UI/UX, visual art direction, game design, conversational AI, conversation psychology, life-design methodology, and privacy/AI safety; their project-specific stances are distinct, but statechart/data-integrity engineering is absent.

The donor diagnosis in `.loom/design/prompt-architecture-brief.md` is supported by current code: `lib/interview/templates.ts` is a fixed four-question Wave 1; `app/api/wave/route.ts` uses `MAX_WAVES=4` and `MAX_QUESTIONS=19`; `lib/ai/interviewer.ts` contains inline v1 prompt text and whole 3-5-question batches; `lib/ai/sensemaker/wave.ts` clears placeholder evidence ids and `build-wave-patch.ts` builds heuristic memory; `lib/ai/sensemaker/final.ts` can synthesize complete fallback lives and `no-evidence`; `package.json` has no XState dependency.

The stable donor surfaces are concrete and inspectable: `prisma/schema.prisma` stores guest sessions, consent, answers, uploads/chunks, derived content, WorkingMemory, Wave and ModelCallLog; `tests/integration/guest-session.test.ts` and `upload-boundary.test.ts` name the isolation/cleanup/upload behaviors TASK-008 promises to preserve. Tests were not executed because their global setup deletes database rows and the Keeper was instructed not to mutate anything beyond the recorded result.

A responsible first engineering action would be donor inventory followed by a contract-first state/persistence slice, but no first edit can be selected until the event transition, revision identity and readiness semantics above are frozen. The intended completion artifact is a versioned Zod event/contract layer, XState machine, Prisma migration/persistence adapter and runnable contract/integration tests; the current Task does not yet specify reproducible commands that execute all of those tests.
